newsitem.title: UK: British Post Office reports record pre-tax profits.
newsitem.headline: British Post Office reports record pre-tax profits.

text.p: Britain's Post Office, seen as a potential target of the government's privatisation programme, on Tuesday announced a rise in annual pretax profits to 577 million pounds ($960 million) in 1996/97 from 422 million the previous year.

The chairman of The Post Office, Michael Heron, who also announced his decision to retire at the end of current year, said the increase in profits was a direct result of a postage price rise effected last year.
Heron said 285 million pounds has gone straight to the state Treasury while a further 216 million will be paid in Corporation Tax.
Postage prices have now been frozen, until at least April 1998.
Annual turnover was 6.37 billion pounds compared with the previous year's 6.21 billion.

The Parcelforce division of the Post Office, however, lost 21 million pounds last year, mainly due to a one-day strike by Communication Workers' Union members in Royal Mail last summer, the company said.
The Post Office also said 400 new jobs would be created in Sunderland by the development of a new telephone call-handling centre for SSL, its telebusiness and customer management business.
Heron underlined the need for a "fundamental change" in the relationship between the Post Office and the government, saying it needed more commercial freedom to make most of new opportunities.

"We need to move quickly. Many leading postal administrations have already taken up the challenge. The Dutch, Danes and Swedes are already wresting the initiative away from us by successfully negotiating greater commercial freedom with their government", he said.
